objective: Extend HACT from synthetic traffic savings to executable software-change verification with conservative publication and measured feedback latency.
baseline: HACT v1.0; pooled ordered certificate tree; default/full and history-only test order.
hypotheses: Change-conditioned, intervention-derived test ordering reduces work to first genuine failure without authorizing selective PASS.
Conditioning certificate layout on actual completion frontiers reduces update traffic; switching overhead may erase the gain.
Arbitrary learned-edge omissions cannot produce PASS through a strict complete-registry gate.
scope: Local CPU-only experiments, immutable copied snapshots, no paid API calls or deployment.
non_goals: No claim of autonomous repair quality or live LLM evaluation.
No claim of complete causal discovery.
No bypass of tests on the strength of learned impact alone.
evaluation: Upstream NetworkX and Toolz tests plus uploaded Future Code v1.2 tests. Predefined mutation operator split by site; survivors and timeouts retained. Separate timing validation from trace replay.
metrics: actual certificate bytes and rebuild costs
stop_conditions: no writes outside private copied snapshots
approval: Local reversible copies and tests authorized by user.
known_limit: Container DNS failed for a public benchmark download; use locally installed upstream packages and retain their sources and versions.
scope_amendment_before_outcomes: SymPy excluded before baseline: its upstream root conftest requires unavailable hypothesis. Replaced with Toolz, preserving unmodified upstream suites.
scope_amendment_core: Full Future Code suite independently passed 263/263 in 26.59 seconds. Mutation campaign is scoped to six core test files to avoid repeating unrelated external-process and transport tests. This scope is frozen before mutation selection/outcomes.
mutation_design: For each of 17 predefined source files select up to 6 distinct AST sites by fixed seeded hash; alternate train/test (up to 3 each). Relational boundary changes, arithmetic replacement, Boolean constant inversion, not-removal. No outcome-based replacement; timeouts/collection errors/survivors retained.
